why: B437: deleting a connection takes its whole wait. In the app a deleted connection's id never comes back. Also B593: a question dated later than the one waiting on the same pane is a new question (answered and asked again between two polls): its own episode, grace and announcement. why: B437: deleting a connection takes its whole wait. The machine withdraws its waiting card at the delete and clears its entries and its announced record; the Swift monitor cleared only the prompts it had posted and redrew the card from the entries left (posting a fresh card for the connection it deleted), left a pushed card it never posted up, and kept the record, so a script that tracks the same connection again had the card withdrawn only once a later poll re-adopted it. In the app a deleted connection's id never comes back. Also B660: a waiting entry lasts until its question is answered or resolved, or its pane or agent ends, capped at six hours; the Swift monitor's set expired it at fifteen minutes, so entries stand longer and a card is withdrawn when its question is answered rather than silently outliving its entry.

In the app a deleted connection's id never comes back.

why: B437: deleting a connection takes its whole wait. The machine withdraws its waiting card at the delete and clears its entries and its announced record; the Swift monitor cleared only the prompts it had posted and redrew the card from the entries left (posting a fresh card for the connection it deleted), left a pushed card it never posted up, and kept the record, so a script that tracks the same connection again had the card withdrawn only once a later poll re-adopted it. In the app a deleted connection's id never comes back. Also B591: a prompt whose grace ran out while its pane was on screen is acknowledged, not posted (a banner and sound for the question the person was looking at, withdrawn by the same sweep); a copy the push recorded for it is seen too. The Swift monitor posted and withdrew it. Also B660: a waiting entry lasts until its question is answered or resolved, or its pane or agent ends, capped at six hours; the Swift monitor's set expired it at fifteen minutes, so entries stand longer and a card is withdrawn when its question is answered rather than silently outliving its entry.

why: B437: deleting a connection takes its whole wait. The machine withdraws its waiting card at the delete and clears its entries and its announced record; the Swift monitor cleared only the prompts it had posted and redrew the card from the entries left (posting a fresh card for the connection it deleted), left a pushed card it never posted up, and kept the record, so a script that tracks the same connection again had the card withdrawn only once a later poll re-adopted it. In the app a deleted connection's id never comes back. Also B593: a question dated later than the one waiting on the same pane is a new question (answered and asked again between two polls): its own episode, grace and announcement. The Swift monitor kept the first one's date, so the second went unannounced.

why: B437: deleting a connection takes its whole wait. The machine withdraws its waiting card at the delete and clears its entries and its announced record; the Swift monitor cleared only the prompts it had posted and redrew the card from the entries left (posting a fresh card for the connection it deleted), left a pushed card it never posted up, and kept the record, so a script that tracks the same connection again had the card withdrawn only once a later poll re-adopted it. In the app a deleted connection's id never comes back.

why: B450: a second question on a pane whose first one's entry still stood is a new wait, and rings. The waiting set's edge counted that pane's own earlier entry as someone waiting, and the second question came in silent. Every moved line is one waiting card that was passive and silent now time-sensitive with its sound, checked by a script against the machine's transcripts before and after. Also B591: a prompt whose grace ran out while its pane was on screen is acknowledged, not posted (a banner and sound for the question the person was looking at, withdrawn by the same sweep); a copy the push recorded for it is seen too. The Swift monitor posted and withdrew it. Also B593: a question dated later than the one waiting on the same pane is a new question (answered and asked again between two polls): its own episode, grace and announcement. The Swift monitor kept the first one's date, so the second went unannounced. Also B660: a waiting entry lasts until its question is answered or resolved, or its pane or agent ends, capped at six hours; the Swift monitor's set expired it at fifteen minutes, so entries stand longer and a card is withdrawn when its question is answered rather than silently outliving its entry.
